hook: Did Count Dracula arrive at Baker Street to hire Sherlock Holmes?

sections.voiceover: Did Count Dracula arrive at Baker Street to hire Sherlock Holmes?
sections.visual_cue: Historical 19th-century London street illustration showing Baker Street in fog.
sections.animation_cue: Fade in from black with slow zoom on the doorway.

sections.voiceover: Author Christian Klaver's Classified Dossier series features this exact meeting. Novelist Loren D. Estleman penned Sherlock Holmes vs Dracula or the Adventure of the Sanguinary Count. Where did these Victorian literary crossovers begin?
sections.visual_cue: Vintage book covers and archival manuscript pages displayed on a wooden desk.
sections.animation_cue: Slide right to reveal manuscript text.

sections.voiceover: However, University of Pennsylvania Press published Daniel Cottom analyzing Sherlock Holmes Meets Dracula.
sections.visual_cue: University press publication title page in academic typography.

sections.voiceover: Sherlockian.net documents Arthur Conan Doyle writing The Sussex Vampire where Holmes investigated suspected supernatural elements. These gothic myth crossovers unite two iconic literary worlds.
sections.visual_cue: Archival photograph of Arthur Conan Doyle and early vampire fiction illustrations.
sections.sfx_cue: Clock ticking softly in the background.

sections.voiceover: Count Dracula met Sherlock Holmes in Victorian fiction.
